facts.fact: The World Bank's eGabon status report records 2 selected hospitals with the National Health Information System installed and operational on 1 March 2025, up from 0 on 16 September 2024, against a target of 13 by August 2025; it does not name the hospitals or their tier.

The World Bank reports the system operational in 2 of 13 selected hospitals on 1 March 2025 and names no primary clinic using it; the share of health workers who regularly use and update the patient's electronic medical record during consultations stood at 0% against a 70% target for August 2025, the Bank noting the target is expected once the system is in place.

The World Bank reports that between September 2024 and March 2025 the system went from 0 to 2 operational hospitals, that prescriptions transmitted electronically remained at 0% against a 60% target, and that full scale-up was expected by project closing on 29 August 2025.

The World Bank reports that the system is built under Component 1 of the eGabon project (US$42.48 million of a US$56 million IBRD loan, 67.81% disbursed by May 2025, closing 29 August 2025); no domestic budget line is mentioned.
The World Bank names the Ministry of the Digital Economy and the national commission CN-TIPPEE as the project's implementing agencies as of May 2025; the health ministry is not named as owner.

systems.owner: implementing agencies: Ministry of the Digital Economy and CN-TIPPEE; World Bank IBRD loan
systems.tiers: 2 of 13 selected hospitals operational on 1 March 2025; Estuaire province hospitals 100% cabled, equipped and interconnected to host it

systems.system: Telemedicine capability in selected medical centres
systems.tiers: 6 selected medical centres equipped and operational since 30 November 2023 (target 6)

note: Classed emr because the project's own indicators measure use of the patients' electronic medical record during consultations and electronic prescriptions. The tier value is a reading: the document says only 'selected hospitals'. owner:ministry stands for the digital economy ministry, not the health ministry. Other figures stated: 2,200 of 3,500 health professionals trained to use the computer tool (63%), 73 IT managers and technicians trained, hospital IT staff trained to operate the system 0% against 100%.
